rules.title: Prohibition on Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with attorney's fees to a prevailing party.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation); damages, injunctive relief, restitution, attorney's fees
rules.effective_date_note: Ordinance text states no effective date; passed to print Nov 18, 2025 (adoption expected Dec 2, 2025 per URL). Other sources may give a different date.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in this document; other sources publish differing dates (e.g., March 1, 2026 vs. January 2026). This ordinance amends an existing chapter 13.63.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, market research for financing, appraisals, and software research/testing/training.

rules.title: Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions to rent or end a tenancy. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.
citation_aliases: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection; fines $1,000-$10,000 per violation
rules.effective_date_note: Document states City Council passed the ordinance April 14, 2020; effective date not stated.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages (actual damages or three times one month's rent), punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner lives; units under a rental agreement allowing owner move-back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, the yearly rent increase (Annual General Adjustment) follows a CPI-based formula set by the Rent Board but can never exceed 5%. Landlords with banked unused adjustments may still raise rent above 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – just cause eviction and notice requirements (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units may evict only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rental debt under one month of HUD Fair Market Rent or for refusing to sign a new fixed-term lease. Lease-breach evictions need a specific notice, substantial actual harm and unreasonable tenant conduct. Termination notices must point to the Rent Board and be filed with it within 3 business days.

rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”)

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act

rules.title: AB 325 - Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software or methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or set prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices or terms. Applies to all pricing, including rents.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data as part of restraint of trade or with coercion
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter
rules.effective_date_note: Document gives no effective date; approved by Governor Oct 6, 2025 as a non-urgency statute, so general effective date of Jan 1, 2026 (computed, consistent with the organizer-known date).
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm; not limited to housing; excludes end consumers.
rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of other antitrust laws.
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act violation; digest notes violations are punishable as a crime.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the landlord may only end the tenancy for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault terminations, the landlord must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance (within 15 days of notice) or waive the final month's rent.
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy
rules.effective_date_note: Section became operative April 1, 2024 per subdivision (m); amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. Repealed as of 2030-01-01.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; relocation = 1 month's rent for no-fault
rules.penalty: Noncompliant termination notice is void; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x damages for willful violations, plus punitive damages; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunctive relief.
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; certain nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner-occupant; single-family owner-occupied (up to two rooms/units rented); owner-occupied duplex; housing with CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property (e.g., single-family homes/condos) owned by non-REIT/corp/LLC-with-corp-member owner with written exemption notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies where tenant has occupied 12+ months (or 24 months if additional adults added); does not apply where a local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a later local ordinance that is more protective; a property is not subject to both.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property (single-family/condo) with non-corporate owner and exemption notice

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, with at most two increments. Initial rent on a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Current version operative April 1, 2024 (effective Jan 1, 2024); the cap originally applied to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (AB 1482).
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (not mobilehomes); certain separately alienable properties (single-family homes, condos) with non-corporate/non-REIT owners and written notice; owner-occupied duplexes; mobilehome homeowners.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property generally, unless exempt.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where local rent control restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.).
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to 3x damages if willful; enforceable by the Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate, non-REIT owners with written notice

rules.title: California residential security deposit limits and handling
rules.requirement: Landlords may not demand or receive security of more than one month's rent (two months if the landlord is a natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total; not for service members). rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security for rental agreements of residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.

All 1-4 unit properties are exempt; landlords must apply to the city for certain rent increases (capital improvement, hardship), and tenants can petition over illegal rent or failure to maintain service.
citation_aliases: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
rules.quoted_span: (Please Note: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control)
rules.key_value: Rent control for buildings with 5+ units
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt; other exemptions can be requested through a Rent Control Exemption Request.

unverifiable_exemptions: other permitted exemptions granted through Rent Control Exemption Request

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a covered tenancy without just cause (at-fault reasons or no-fault reasons such as owner move-in, demolition, or government order). No-fault evictions generally require relocation assistance to the tenant.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions

unverifiable_exemptions: some non-profit homeless facilities or treatment centers
tenant has not lived in unit six months or original lease not expired

rules.coverage_conditions: Covers most residential properties in the City of LA not regulated by the RSO; applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first. Can apply to buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and to a single single-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless/treatment facilities, some HACLA or government-owned properties.
rules.interaction: RSO units are covered by the RSO's own just-cause rules; JCO covers units not under the RSO. Supersedes state Civ. Code § 1946.2 for covered units.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in document.
rules.conflict_note: State law (Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2) may overlap; local JCO is the stricter local rule.

rules.title: Los Angeles eviction for non-payment limited to rent above Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for unpaid rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size. This applies to all RSO and JCO units.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Eviction for Non-Payment of Rent (Fair Market Rent threshold)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all RSO and JCO rental units.
rules.key_value: Rent owed must exceed Fair Market Rent for the bedroom size

rules.title: Los Angeles eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: Every eviction notice served on a tenant must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service. Landlords must also post and provide a Notice of Right to Counsel.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Eviction Notice Filing Requirement (LAHD)
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all JCO and RSO rental properties.
rules.key_value: File within 3 business days of service

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance - allowable rent increases
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised only once every 12 months by the allowable percentage set by LAHD. Since Feb 2, 2026, no extra percentage for utilities and no 10% for an added dependent; 10% for an added non-dependent tenant is still allowed.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months; allowable annual percentage set by LAHD

rules.exemptions: Condos/townhomes with tenancies commenced after 12/31/1995 not rent-regulated; luxury exemption; temporary exemptions.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO - just cause eviction, notice filing and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenants can be evicted only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service, and no-fault evictions require relocation assistance and a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict.

City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO

three (3) business days of service on the tenant

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, the annual allowable rent increase was 3% for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Beginning February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add any extra percentage for utilities. RSO and SCEP surcharges may be passed through only after the unit is registered and written notice is given.
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, art. 1 (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Beginning February 2, 2026, a landlord can no longer include any additional percentage increase for utilities
rules.key_value: 3% annual increase (7/1/2025–6/30/2026); no utility add-on from 2/2/2026
rules.effective_date_note: Date the removal of the utility add-on takes effect, per LAHD page; the 3% figure applies from 2025-07-01. Another source (landlord association) has reported 2026-01-24.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the RSO; check ZIMAS to confirm.
rules.interaction: The state Tenant Protection Act cap does not apply where local rent control is stricter.
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates exist for the new formula: 2026-02-02 (LAHD) and 2026-01-24 (landlord association). The 3% figure covers only through 2026-06-30, so the current-year figure is not stated in this document.

rules.title: LA RSO/JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions from units covered by the RSO or JCO, landlords must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving a termination notice. A copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 days of service, and payment must be made available within 15 days of service.

All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a

rules.requirement: Owners demolishing Protected Units for new construction must pay enhanced relocation to lower-income households, under one of three options. Tenants may remain until 6 months before construction starts and have return and first-refusal rights.

rules.title: State bar on local rent control
rules.requirement: Cities and towns in Massachusetts may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally compensated regulation for owners of 10 or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less.

rules.title: MA Fair Housing Law: unlawful practices incl. source-of-income / voucher discrimination

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can keep the tenancy by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, on or before the answer day in an eviction action. If the nonpayment was caused by a government delay in mailing or delivering a rent or subsistence payment, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent is paid in that time.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will (tenancy at will termination notice)
rules.requirement: A landlord or tenant must give three months' written notice to end a tenancy at will (or the rent-payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, if rent is paid at intervals under three months). For nonpayment of rent, 14 days' written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not had a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days; the notice must include a statutory statement of that right.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (30 days min. if rent paid more often); 14 days' notice to quit for nonpayment, 10-day right to cure
rules.effective_date_note: Document gives no effective date for this long-standing section.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies at will.
rules.penalty: If the notice omits the required cure-right notification, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in any possession action.

rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for reporting code violations, enforcing housing laws in court, or organizing or joining a tenants' union. Violators owe damages of 1 to 3 months' rent (or actual damages if greater) plus attorney's fees. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months of such activity is presumed to be a reprisal.

rules.title: Broker fees payable only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may contract solely with either the tenant or the landlord, and any fee must be paid only by the party who originally engaged the broker. A landlord who hires the broker cannot shift the broker's fee to the tenant.
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Text as amended by 2025, 9, Sec. 43 effective August 1, 2025 (see 2025, 9, Sec. 136).
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent: required form and statement
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must come with a state form that documents any repayment agreements and gives information on rental assistance, court rules, and legal restrictions on evictions. It must state that the notice is not an eviction and only a court order can force you to leave. Courts will not accept a summary process filing for nonpayment without proof the form was delivered.
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.key_value: Notice to quit for nonpayment must be accompanied by state form; no court filing without proof of delivery
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to written notices to quit for nonpayment of rent given to residential tenants.
rules.penalty: Courts will not accept for filing a summary process complaint without proof of delivery of the form.

rules.title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on applications or orally/in writing before making a conditional offer. They may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods. Any withdrawal needs written reasons and an individualized assessment.
rules.key_value: No criminal-history inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th)
